title: The First Recorded Strike in History
notes: Register: matter-of-fact, slightly wry. The wryness lives in the record's own details (55 cakes, the scribe's smaller ration, the ox in the stable); the animation can let them land, but never winks. Play the turn, s45 to s47, completely straight.

The workmen, Amennakhte and Mentmose are vague-faced cartoons in front of generic backdrops (a desert ridge, a guard post, a wall at the edge of the fields). Nothing generated depicts the village of Deir el-Medina, a specific temple, the tomb or the valley: those are always the real photographs and the maps.
Every archival image is a document, an object, or a photograph of a place as it is now or as it was in the 19th or early 20th century. Every one is captioned so it does not read as ancient.

The Strike Papyrus (p02, Cat. 1880) is the primary source and returns many times. It is CC0 from the Museo Egizio. Cite it on screen and in the description. Every passage from it is paraphrased, except the one line at s47.
p22 is the verso of the map papyrus, the side that carries the hymn signed by Amennakhte. The recto (p20) is the map: very wide, letterbox it, never crop.

Ostracon S. 9611 (p17) is a court testimony by a workman named Menna from the same reign. It is shown as an example of village writing; its caption never says it is Penanuke's statement. p08 is an accounting flake of the same kind, not from the strike.
The conspiracy against Ramesses III (s54) is never drawn; it is the Judicial Papyrus photograph only. The vizier To appears only as his sealed letter.
Pronunciation notes for Chirp are at the top of narration.md.
Music is null for the build. If a bed is added in the edit, nothing under the turn (s43 to s50); a low, sparse bed may enter at s54.
LOW RESOLUTION: p06 (1032x670). Native size only.
Every archival URL was resolved from the Commons API.
Guide objects: the scribe's palette (s06, s13, s49) and the half-full grain measure (s18, s42).

amennakhte.desc: Amennakhte, scribe of the Tomb around 1157 BC: a lean Egyptian man in a pleated linen kilt and short wig, a scribe's palette under his arm, simple vague face

workmen.desc: the crew of tomb workmen around 1157 BC: a group of Egyptian craftsmen in short linen kilts, some with headcloths, carrying chisels and baskets, simple vague faces, drawn as a group

mentmose.desc: Mentmose, chief of the necropolis police around 1157 BC, a broad Egyptian man with a staff and a linen cloak, simple vague face

crowd.desc: extras: water and firewood carriers with donkeys, Egyptian officials and scribes in long linen robes, a workman with his hand raised in an oath, the mayor of Thebes carried past, an accuser counting on his fingers, simple vague faces

sets.desert_ridge: a pale desert ridge in Upper Egypt under a hard blue sky, a footpath along the crest, a few small rough stone shelters, no buildings of note
sets.map_thebes: a large vintage parchment map of a stretch of the Nile, a band of farmland on the west bank, pale desert hills beyond, unmarked
sets.farmland_edge: the edge where pale desert meets green fields and palm trees, a long plain mudbrick wall running along it, bright sun
sets.guard_post: a small mudbrick guard post beside a desert track, a low wall, long shadows
sets.map_desert: a large vintage parchment map of Upper Egypt from the Nile to the Red Sea across the Eastern Desert, unmarked
sets.museum: a quiet museum gallery with long glass cases under soft light, a polished floor

props.grain_heaps: two small heaps of grain on a reed mat, one of husked emmer wheat and one of barley
props.grain_sack: a coarse woven sack of grain
props.measures_three: three plain wooden grain measures of different sizes standing in a row, each filled with emmer wheat
props.palette: a scribe's wooden palette with two ink wells, one red and one black, three reed pens beside it
props.copper_tools: a few copper chisels and a mallet
props.lamp_wicks: a bundle of twisted linen lamp wicks beside a small clay lamp
props.flake_writing: a flat flake of pale limestone covered in neat rows of black ink marks that cannot be read
props.measure_half: a plain wooden grain measure filled only halfway with emmer wheat, a few loose grains around its base
props.letter_sealed: a rolled papyrus letter tied with cord and sealed with a small lump of clay
props.circles: two thin ink circles on old papyrus, one slightly larger and set a little off centre so they no longer line up
props.cakes: a heap of small round flat cakes on a reed tray
props.oil_jar: a small stoppered pottery jar of oil with a faint sheen on the rim
props.door_bolt: a plain wooden door in a whitewashed mudbrick wall, a short wooden bolt across it
props.two_sacks: two coarse woven sacks of grain set down on bare ground
props.ox: a brown ox in a stable, a plain mark branded on its flank
props.stone_chips: a pile of fresh stone chips and a chisel
